answer: Special Ops canyon rule: pay the work, not the headcount. Each epoch the ledger posts a fixed set of 200 sealed tasks, each locked by a cipher hash of its correct output, so answers are checked automatically. A task pays once, to whoever cracks it first, then closes. Spinning up 1,000 keys never grows the pie; they just wander the same canyon of 200 tasks, so a farm earns exactly what its raw skill would earn under one name. Splitting into fakes buys only overhead.
